text:
sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 in three stages: reading, conversion, and upload.

A reader process connects to Postgres and streams rows in batches. This limits memory use and lets later stages start work before the full query finishes.

A converter turns each batch into a Parquet row group. Parquet stores data in a column format. As a result, later queries can read only the columns they need.

An uploader writes the row groups to S3 as multipart objects. If a part fails, the uploader retries that part and does not restart the whole upload.

Each stage runs on its own and passes batches to the next stage through a queue. This lets the reader, the converter, and the uploader work at the same time.
